query_preview:
/Saturday through Wednesday/... 
A short drying period will move in on Saturday, but higher level
moisture and clouds will be increasing throughout the day. We 
can't rule out a few light showers on Saturday, but with little to
no instability and drier air in the mid levels little if any 
additional accumulating rainfall is expected through at least the 
afternoon. Some guidance is showing shower activity to begin 
already in the evening, but for most areas it should hold off 
until after midnight.

Attention then turns toward one of our stronger Arv that can
affect the Desert Southwest moving in Saturday night and lasting
through much of Sunday. The AR will also coincide with a fairly 
strong shortwave trough developing west of northern Baja on 
Saturday before tracking right through the southern half of 
Arizona during the daytime hours Sunday. This weather event is
shaping up to be a classic El Nino season AR event which would
normally occur from late December through February. All of the
ingredients for a prolonged moderate rainfall event look to be
there on Sunday with an impressive 18 hours of 35-50kt
southwesterly upslope H8-H7 flow and at least 12 hours of strong 
jet forced ascent. These impressive forcing mechanisms will also 
line up with record or near record moisture levels for this time 
of year with PWATs rising to 300-350% of normal. Instability will 
be lacking with MUCAPEs at most 200-300 J/kg, but the long 
duration of the rain will make up for the lack of higher rainfall 
rates. 

We expect showers to blossom first over the high terrain northeast
of Phoenix sometime in the evening before filling in across most 
of south-central Arizona around or just after midnight. Showers 
will stay somewhat scattered through the overnight hours before 
becoming widespread over much of Arizona by mid morning Sunday. As
the main shortwave begins to track through southern California 
later Sunday morning, a fairly solid shield of light to moderate 
rain should move through southern California and then through 
Arizona Sunday afternoon. Upslope showers should persist over 
portions of south-central Arizona into the high terrain into 
Sunday evening, but the activity should be gradually winding down.

Expected rainfall rates on Sunday are not all that high, but rain
totals will add up over time as this event will last longer than
our typical weather events. Based on the record moisture levels, 
strong forcing, but little instability rainfall rates will 
generally be in the 0.1-0.2"/hr range in the Phoenix area to as 
high as 0.2-0.3"/hr in the high terrain north and east of the 
Phoenix area. Fairly steady light to moderate rainfall is expected
from just before sunrise through the afternoon in the 
aforementioned areas with rainfall totals averaging 1-1.5" in 
Phoenix to 2-3" over the higher terrain. Believe it our not, the 
NBM is also suggesting the possibility (25%) of rainfall totals 
over 2" in the Phoenix to as much as 3-4" in the high terrain. 
Much lower rainfall totals of 0.25-0.5" are expected over the 
lower deserts of southwest Arizona and southeast California due to
some rain-shadowing effects and the lack of upslope forcing.

Even if the average forecast rainfall totals come to fruition on
Sunday, the bulk of the rain will runoff as it will be falling on
already saturated soils. In turn another Flood Watch has been
issued for a large area of south-central AZ, and the eastern AZ 
high terrain starting Sunday, into Monday morning. During this 
time we anticipate the potential for many of the washes filling or
overflowing, and flooding in some of the larger creeks and rivers
as all of the expected rain works through the water basins.

Dry air will begin to filter into the region from the northwest
later on Sunday, overspreading the bulk of the area by Monday 
morning. We may have some lingering showers across the eastern 
1/3rd of Arizona Sunday night into Monday morning, but additional
rainfall amounts should be fairly light. The rest of Monday will
bring decreasing clouds as the drier air works into the region
while another follow-on shortwave trough moves southeastward into
northern New Mexico. Temperatures for both Sunday and Monday will
be fairly cool with highs as low as the lower 70s for the Phoenix
area to maybe the mid to upper 70s across the western lower 
deserts. Upper level ridging is then forecast to mostly take over 
across the Desert Southwest going into the middle part of next 
week, but temperatures will be fairly slow to rise with readings 
staying below normal.
